newsitem.title: ITALY: Snam leads way for Italy's Eni in H1.
newsitem.headline: Snam leads way for Italy's Eni in H1.

text.p: Snam, the natural gas unit of Italy's Eni Ente Nazionale Idrocarburi SpA, saw the biggest jump in profits of all the energy giant's operating units in the first half of the year, a company document said.

The prospectus for the forthcoming second tranche sale of Eni stock, said Snam recorded a net profit of 841 billion lire in the first six months of the year, up from 554 billion lire in the same period in 1995.
It said the rise was largely due to an increase of some 900 million cubic metres in gas sales.
The only unit to provide a larger net profit for Eni was exploration and production arm Agip SpA, which had a first half net of 949 billion lire, down 44 billion on 1995.

Eni, which currently has 15 percent of its shares quoted and is due to offer another chunk of stock to the public on October 21, reported first half consolidated net profits of 2.758 trillion lire earlier this week.

In a breakdown of its various sectors, the sale prospectus said Eni's refining and marketing unit, Agip Petroli, chalked up a 338 billion lire loss in the first half from a previous two billion lire net profit.

Eni blamed the loss on the fact that it has adopted the U.S. accounting system SFAS 121, which led it to reduce the estimated worth of its refineries by 549 billion lire. The new system also hurt the Agip results, Eni said.

Petrol chemicals unit EniChem saw its net profit cut by almost 50 percent to 446 billion lire from 853 billion, with the company stung by a 20 percent reduction in sales prices as well as by lira gains.
